title: How Lionel Messi's Players to Watch From 2024, 2025 Have Fared
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 17, 2026Lionel Messi has tipped several Argentinian hotshots for great things. / Luis ROBAYO/AFP/Getty ImagesThe twilight of Lionel Messi’s glittering career has thrust him into conversations that transcend mere greatness.

After inspiring Argentina to World Cup glory in 2022, Messi, at the age of 39, almost single-handedly guided a distinctly flawed Albiceleste side at the end of its tether to back-to-back successes on the biggest stage. He subsequently bade a dignified farewell to the national team this fall and is continuing to dominate Major League Soccer with Inter Miami.

For all his majesty, Messi has seldom portrayed himself as a soccer obsessive. You couldn’t imagine him churning out a multi-hour Football Manager session, for example, or even tuning into a match in which he doesn’t have a vested interest.

Yet adidas would lead you to believe that Messi is spending his downtime, of which he does have more of nowadays, watching AZ Alkmaar’s latest Eredivisie encounter, keeping tabs on their exciting young midfielder, Kees Smit.

Smit is one of the 10 rising stars backed by Messi in adidas’s latest campaign. The Argentinian great has provided such lists sporadically since 2015; the latest batch of rising stars follows two sets of 10 offered in both 2024 and 2025.

It may be too soon to discern whether Messi—or rather adidas, given that the players included are all adidas-sponsored—“knows ball,” as the chronically online generation would say. Nevertheless, enough time has elapsed to gauge whether he/they were onto something.
Here’s a breakdown of how Messi’s tipped future stars from the previous two years have since fared.

Ndala didn’t make the grade at Manchester City. / Bradley Collyer/PA Images/Getty ImagesJoel Ndala joined Manchester City in 2017 and garnered plenty of buzz after a string of impressive performances for England at the U-17 World Cup in 2023.

The winger travelled with Pep Guardiola’s senior team on its preseason tour the following summer, but joined PSV Eindhoven at the end of the transfer window. The Dutch club, however, didn’t fulfill their obligation to buy, and Ndala, who struggled in PSV’s reserves for half a season, subsequently endured forgettable loan spells at Nottingham Forest, Hull City and Sheffield Wednesday.
He failed to make a single Premier League appearance during his loan spells, and even had his Wednesday loan terminated early due to disciplinary issues.
The 20-year-old joined Belgian club Cercle Brugge for an undisclosed fee in the summer.

Messi showed some love for his young compatriot. / Matt McNulty/Getty ImagesThere’s much for Argentinians to be exciting about in a post-Messi world, but it remains unclear whether the once-highly regarded Claudio Echeverri will be part of the Albiceleste’s long-term plans.
Nicknamed "El Diablito" (little devil) for his impish playmaking abilities, Echeverri grew up idolizing Messi but failed to share the field with his hero before the 39-year-old’s retirement.

Manchester City had great success converting River Plate’s Julián Alvarez into a star, and they perhaps thought that Echeverri would embark on a similar path once he wound up in Pep Guardiola’s grasp. The creative midfielder remains on City’s books, but he’s still trying to find himself on European soil.
Echeverri had rather uninspired loan spells at Bayer Leverkusen and Girona, and is spending the 2026–27 campaign with Benfica. The early signs haven’t been promising.

Juventus‘ No. 10. / MARCO BERTORELLO/AFP/Getty ImagesKenan Yıldız was already well-established when he received Messi’s endorsement. The Turkish starlet dazzled for Juventus’ Next Gen outfit and made his debut for the first team in 2023.

Yıldız was a hit right away, becoming the club’s youngest foreign goalscorer and taking the club’s venerated No. 10 shirt previously worn by the likes of Alessandro Del Piero, Roberto Baggio and Paulo Dybala.
You wouldn’t say superstardom has been acquired yet, but the sharpshooting Yıldız is well on his way.

Shaw made USWNT history in 2024. / Brad Smith/ISI Photos/USSF/Getty ImagesEmma Hayes’s snub of Jaedyn Shaw for the USWNT’s October matches garnered plenty of attention, even if the manager assured that the Gotham FC forward remains central to her plans.
